Naples ’44
About Timeline Places People Folklore Themes

Theme

Bureaucracy & absurdity

Military/administrative farce, red tape, false alarms

Appears in 30 diary entries.

  1. September 8 1943
    Aboard ship off Italy, news arrives of the armistice; Lewis notes the total lack of intelligence about what awaits them at Salerno.
    • War & violence
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  2. September 15 1943
    A comrade's harrowing return from Salerno; confusion persists as officers and men lose track of each other amid ongoing shelling.
    • War & violence
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  3. September 21 1943
    Ordered back to the idle beachhead life at Paestum despite its pointlessness; the section finally gets a small, real intelligence task that evening.
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
    • Personal reflection
  4. October 8 1943
    Floods of dubious civilian tips overwhelm the section, including a "spy" who turns out to be rumored a witch by superstitious villagers.
    • Superstition & religion
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  5. October 10 1943
    Amid the grim work of processing denunciations, Lewis is struck by the vivid street life and rituals of a working-class Neapolitan neighborhood.
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
    • Naples's character
  6. October 13 1943
    A week of fruitless "spy scares" turns up only harmless eccentrics, while a new bureaucracy of mail and phone censorship intercepts trivia.
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  7. October 23 1943
    A false tip about mass delayed-action mines triggers a chaotic mass evacuation of Naples, including hospital patients and the bedridden.
    • War & violence
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  8. October 24 1943
    Lewis is sent to investigate whether the German soldier behind the mine hoax should be executed as a spy.
    • War & violence
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  9. November 1 1943
    Lewis is indignant at the drastic cut to informant funds, arguing money isn't really what motivates their most dedicated Italian contacts.
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
    • Personal reflection
  10. December 5 1943
    Lewis avoids an unwanted arrest by spending the day on unrelated errands, reflecting on the unit's discomfort with being used for private vendettas.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  11. December 18 1943
    Lewis describes how gullible unit commanders and their local interpreters get dragged into baseless denunciations and village feuds, including against a corrupt police marshal.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  12. January 1 1944
    A tedious, unproductive investigation into telephone-wire theft, which the Army wrongly treats as sabotage rather than opportunistic copper theft.
    • Black market
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  13. January 12 1944
    The wire-theft crackdown continues to unfairly target small, desperate offenders like an elderly scrap-merchant, while real traders go untouched.
    • Poverty & hunger
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  14. January 14 1944
    Amid a flood of usually-worthless rumors, one turns out to be true — an imminent Anzio landing — sending Lewis scrambling to trace a security leak.
    • War & violence
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  15. January 19 1944
    Chaotic, arbitrary court proceedings at Castel Capuano illustrate the absurd unevenness of wartime justice, set against an open black market.
    • Black market
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  16. February 5 1944
    Thieves brazenly strip the wheels from vehicles at the supposedly secure Field Security Headquarters, showcasing local audacity and ingenuity.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  17. March 3 1944
    An account of a bizarre, catastrophic Allied intelligence scheme prompted by fears that prostitution was being used to spread disease among troops.
    • Sex & relationships
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
    • Disease & health
  18. March 5 1944
    The growing, increasingly careless traffic of "line-crossers" and letter-couriers moving between Allied and German territory raises serious security concerns.
    • War & violence
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  19. March 13 1944
    The crackdown on the black market punishes only the powerless, as shown by a farcical smuggling trial that collapses through prosecutorial incompetence.
    • Black market
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  20. May 7 (ii) 1944
    Frustrated by unresolved banditry, the General pressures Italian police into a harsher new anti-bandit operation, which Lewis observes as an onlooker.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  21. May 31 1944
    Post-Fascist Italy's political life fragments into dozens of parties, some espousing bizarre or fringe ideas, reflecting a climate of instability.
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
    • Personal reflection
  22. July 26 1944
    An almost novelistic assignment to escort a mysterious, allegedly dangerous female internee to Rome for interrogation raises awkward questions among the section.
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
    • Personal reflection
  23. August 20 1944
    The local Marshal frets over bandit threats to the town, but Lewis notes how absurdly under-armed and unprepared the local security forces really are.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  24. August 25 1944
    A grenade attack on an MP sergeant prompts a tense but ultimately toothless conference about how to respond to the now-motorized bandits.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  25. September 6 1944
    The generous but reckless Canadians treat everything, including two local girls they've picked up, with careless ease; Lewis is assigned to probe a clandestine political party.
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
    • Allied conduct
  26. September 19 1944
    A tense overnight checkpoint operation against suspected bandit traffic is set up on a lonely road, staffed by a poorly coordinated mix of Allied and Italian forces.
    • Crime & banditry
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  27. October 8 1944
    Mob violence breaks out against local girls seen with Allied soldiers, and the section is controversially ordered to intervene with sub-machine guns.
    • War & violence
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  28. October 16 1944
    A large-scale, coercive round-up of women for VD examinations follows a tip from a gynecologist contact, exposing the harsh methods used to fight the disease.
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
    • Disease & health
  29. October 20 1944
    Official policy strongly discourages marriages between soldiers and Italian civilians, citing poor historical outcomes for such wartime unions.
    • Sex & relationships
    • Bureaucracy & absurdity
  30. October 24 1944
    Lewis is abruptly ordered to a new mission repatriating Russian ex-POWs, sensing this marks the end of his time in Naples.
